paper.title: Code as Policies: Language Model Programs for Embodied Control
paper.central_claim: Few-shot prompted code-writing LLMs can generate executable robot policies that compose perception and control APIs, reason spatially and geometrically, generalize to new instructions and express reactive control without additional model training; recursively generating undefined functions improves robotics-themed and general code generation. Multiple real robot platforms demonstrate the formulation.

sections_read: Appendix C Reasoning with Code vs. Natural Language
Appendix K Simulation Tabletop, Table VI
materials.notes: Verified text SHA-256 against the re-pinned input manifest. PDF extraction contains all appendices, but multi-column tables/code have reading-order artifacts. H-K enumerate API contracts and prompt URLs, not all linked domain-specific prompt contents; external links were not fetched. evidence.locator: Abstract, opening
evidence.quote:
LLMs can take in new commands and autonomously
re-compose API calls to generate new policy code respectively.
evidence.support_explanation: Author's instruction-to-executable-policy generalization claim, not a claim of autonomous policy improvement across evaluated episodes.

evidence.locator: I Introduction, fixed-skill bottleneck
evidence.quote:
incorporating each new skill (and mode of grounding) requires
additional data and retraining
evidence.support_explanation: Motivates composing feedback and continuous primitive parameters rather than choosing only among pretrained skill names.

evidence.locator: II Related Work, nearest adjacent systems
evidence.quote:
Inner Monologue [18]
expands LLM planning by incorporating outputs from success detectors or other visual language models and uses their feedback to
re-plan.
evidence.support_explanation: Author acknowledges adjacent feedback-aware LLM planning. The residual is not simply adding feedback; CaP exposes numerical policy logic and perception-to-control computation. This is the focal paper's account, not independent inspection of Inner Monologue's original version.

evidence.locator: III Method, execution scope and checks
evidence.quote:
ensuring there are no import statements, special variables that
begin with __, or calls to exec and eval.
evidence.support_explanation: A textual/code-execution restriction precedes Python execution. This is not a robot motion-validity checker or proof of a secure sandbox.

evidence.locator: III A, LMP session
evidence.quote:
an
LMP "session" by incrementally appending new instructions and
responses to the prompt
evidence.support_explanation: Within-session linguistic context persists; subsequent instructions can refer to earlier actions. No cross-task success-filtered learning protocol is thereby established.

evidence.locator: III B, default model and decoding
evidence.quote:
use OpenAI Codex code-davinci-002 with
temperature 0
evidence.support_explanation: Default frozen code-writing backbone and deterministic greedy decoding; HumanEval sampling is an explicitly different protocol.

evidence.locator: III C, hierarchical function generation
evidence.quote:
We use the functiongenerating LMP to write these undefined functions and add them
to the scope. This procedure is repeated on the generated function
body, hierarchically creating new functions in a depth-first manner.
evidence.support_explanation: Inspectable recursion and persistence in execution scope, driven by unresolved function names rather than execution-quality feedback or an acceptance test.

evidence.locator: IV Experiments, quantitative versus qualitative scope
evidence.quote:
quantitative evaluations of a robot
system using CaP is limited to a constrained set of simulated tasks
in IV-D
evidence.support_explanation: Explicitly prevents turning real-robot demonstrations into counted success/transfer evidence.

evidence.locator: IV A, RoboCodeGen evaluation
evidence.quote:
our
evaluation metric is the percentage of the generated code that
passes human-written unit tests.
evidence.support_explanation: Offline code correctness is grounded by unit tests; the benchmark contains 37 functions and compares flat/hierarchical generation across four API-accessible models (Table I), not 37 closed-loop robot tasks.

evidence.locator: IV D and Table III, task families and results
evidence.quote: Success rates over task families with 50 trials per task.
evidence.support_explanation: Table III reports CaP long-horizon/spatial-geometric SR: SA-SI 97.20/89.30, UA-SI 97.60/73.33, UA-UI 80.00/62.00 percent. NL planner long-horizon 86.40/88.00/64.00; spatial-geometric marked N/A, not a measured zero. Table VI supplies detailed rows and oracle/no-oracle CLIPort distinction.

evidence.locator: IV D, baseline data and prompting
evidence.quote:
CLIPort [36] policies trained
via imitation learning on 30k demonstrations
evidence.support_explanation: CLIPort comparison has a different data, representation and perception regime; end-to-end versus modular comparison is not a clean code-only causal ablation.

evidence.locator: V Discussion and Limitations
evidence.quote:
Our approach also assumes all given instructions are
feasible, and we cannot tell if a response will be correct a priori.
evidence.support_explanation: No universal correctness or feasibility guarantee; generated program execution remains fallible despite lexical checks.

evidence.locator: Appendix A, prompt engineering and code repair
evidence.quote: we did not employ this method in our experiments.
evidence.support_explanation: In context this refers to LLM editing/fixing code, which the authors found inconsistent. Do not fabricate a verifier-guided program-repair or autonomous self-improvement loop.

evidence.locator: Appendix C, spatial reasoning correctness
evidence.quote:
An LLM-generated answer for position selection is considered
correct if all coordinates are within 1cm of the ground truth.
evidence.support_explanation: A clear tolerance exists for the offline 23-question position-selection benchmark; it must not be silently copied as the success criterion for closed-loop tabletop manipulation. Other set: 28 object-selection questions; Table IV totals 35/58/98 percent for vanilla/CoT/LMP.

evidence.locator: Appendix D, fairer flat-generation prompt control
evidence.quote:
the only difference in the hierarchical prompt is using a
yet-to-be-defined function get_mean instead of calculating the
mean directly.
evidence.support_explanation: A same-backbone flat-prompt control reduces the no-prompt confound. Table V: greedy 45.7 no-prompt, 50.6 flat-prompt, 53.0 hierarchical; sampled P@1 34.9/36.6/39.8 percent. It is not an equal-call-budget embodied hierarchy ablation.

evidence.locator: Appendix D, deployment decoding and unavailable unit tests
evidence.quote:
sampling multiple solutions is not practical for LMPs, which need
to perform tasks in a zero-shot manner without engineering prior
unit tests.
evidence.support_explanation: HumanEval sample-and-test pass rates are not runtime robot candidate selection. Robot programs use the most likely output.

evidence.locator: Appendix F, reactive controller boundary
evidence.quote:
require actually tuning the gains based on execution feedback,
something our method does not support at the moment.
evidence.support_explanation: Toy reactive controller generation is not feedback-driven controller optimization; PD hints and near-upright initialization matter.

evidence.locator: Appendix G, real perception calibration and failure
evidence.quote:
many real-world failures could be
attributed to inaccurate detections.
evidence.support_explanation: Real-world MDETR/ViLD plus depth deprojection need pre-registered camera transforms and domain prompt tuning; perception failures are not enumerated as rates.

evidence.locator: Appendix I, identity boundary
evidence.quote:
we do not have a good
way of persisting the identity of duplicate objects across VLM
detections.
evidence.support_explanation: Unique-object restriction undercuts claims of general scene memory; context/function persistence does not solve tracking.

evidence.locator: Appendix K, simulation input visibility
evidence.quote: via a scripted object detector
evidence.support_explanation: Quantitative simulation exposes object list and positions via a scripted detector plus pick/place primitive. Treat this as privileged structured perception rather than evidence of robust vision grounding.

evidence.locator: Appendix K, definition of seen instructions/attributes
evidence.quote:
the “seen” instructions
or attributes are permitted to appear in the prompt or used for
training
evidence.support_explanation: K explicitly lists seen eight and unseen six instruction templates and attribute values (e.g. unseen diagonal, farthest, lower directions, held-out colors). This is a within-environment conditioning holdout, not new-embodiment validation.

evidence.locator: Appendix K, trial sampling and CLIPort termination
evidence.quote:
A total of 50 trials are
performed per task, each with sampled attributes and initial scene
configurations (block and bowl types, numbers, and positions).
evidence.support_explanation: Repeated trials and denominators exist. CLIPort is separately evaluated with ten-action termination and oracle success termination. No confidence intervals, seed variability or numerical task-specific success checker tolerances are given in K/Table VI.

evidence.locator: Appendix M, cross-embodiment caveat
evidence.quote:
this ability
is brittle with existing LLMs and cannot reliably adapt to APIs
that are very different.
evidence.support_explanation: Omni/unidirectional API-conditioned code example is not counted closed-loop cross-embodiment transfer.

signatures.object: Instruction-to-policy interface: replace a sequence of fixed skill labels with executable Python that processes perceptual outputs and parameterizes low-level APIs.
signatures.information: Frozen code-davinci-002 sees command comments, hand-authored Hints/Examples and object names; code queries positions/boxes/visibility through domain APIs. Real robot uses MDETR/ViLD plus calibrated depth; quantitative simulation uses scripted object detection and object coordinates. No compact student or teacher-student privilege split.
signatures.operation: Generate code; check prohibited constructs; execute in API-provided global scope and variable/function local scope; use NumPy/Shapely for geometry and for/while/if for feedback control.
signatures.output: Executable perception-to-action policy and parameterized primitive calls, not only a prose plan.
signatures.conditions: Meaningful consistent API names/types, calibrated coordinate frames, adequate primitives, suitable prompt examples and feasible instructions.
signatures.feedback: Runtime sensor/API values drive generated program branches; execution feedback is not a scored signal for LLM code repair in the evaluated method.
signatures.selection_rule: Greedy temperature-zero output, lexical restrictions before execution. No success-tested best-of-N policy acceptance gate.
signatures.selection_data: Manually engineered examples; K defines prompt-eligible versus held-out templates/attributes. No autonomous selection dataset.
signatures.persistence: Variables/functions in execution scope and optional session prompt history; no evaluated permanent success-filtered skill bank.
signatures.later_use: Later commands/program calls can reuse prior variables/functions and refer to session history.
signatures.claimed_effect: Spatial-geometric instruction following and generalization without additional robot-policy model training.
signatures.failure_boundary: Perception/primitive coverage, ambiguous types, complex instructions, infeasible requests, no a-priori response correctness; no audited motion-validity guarantee.

signatures.object: Flat code generation and undefined helper-function expansion.
signatures.information: Generated program AST, names already present in scope, function signature/context, few-shot function-generation examples; no unit-test result is exposed as a robot runtime selection signal.
signatures.operation: Find unresolved function calls in the AST, request their definitions from a function-generating LMP, recursively expand child bodies depth-first and add definitions to scope.
signatures.conditions: Backbone must be competent enough to use abstractions; first-party API conventions and types must be inferable.
signatures.feedback: Undefined-name detection is syntactic dependency resolution, not reward or behavioral validation.
signatures.selection_rule: Complete missing definitions using most-likely generation; no verification-guided candidate search demonstrated in deployment.
signatures.selection_data: Flat/hierarchical prompts with two HumanEval example functions; task-test unit tests are evaluation only.
signatures.persistence: Generated helpers added to current execution scope.
signatures.later_use: Parent program and subsequent programs can call these helpers; no isolated longitudinal retained-gain evaluation.
signatures.claimed_effect: Improved RoboCodeGen and HumanEval correctness, especially productive composition for stronger models.
signatures.failure_boundary: Smaller model does not uniformly benefit; controller gain tuning and reliable code repair are unsupported.

retained_claim_trace.reason: Static harness/method claim, not a measured autonomous retained-improvement claim. The text says functions can accumulate and illustrates session history, but does not evaluate selection and retention from scored trials.
retained_claim_trace.before: Fixed provided APIs and hand-engineered prompt examples.
retained_claim_trace.proposed_change: New command-conditioned policy and recursively generated helper definitions.
retained_claim_trace.selection_data_rule: Greedy generation and unresolved-name expansion, not validation-based accept/reject.
retained_claim_trace.persisted_change: Current scope/session only; duration beyond session not evaluated.
retained_claim_trace.later_tasks: Reuse possible and contextual commands illustrated; no independent retained-gain cohort.
retained_claim_trace.measured_gain: Code-generation/within-benchmark task success, not retained or improver improvement.

gap.author_gap: LLM skill planners inherit a data/retraining burden from fixed low-level skills and cannot freely express new perception-action feedback, continuous parameters or precise spatial relations.
gap.checked_gap: Specific and plausible residual at the planner-to-executor boundary: choosing named skills is different from composing code over percepts and numerical control arguments. Acknowledged feedback-aware Inner Monologue means feedback alone is not the gap. Existing perception/control primitives remain required, so CaP reduces but does not eliminate the robot-system engineering/data burden.

gap.residue: Pre-existing skill selection and linguistic feedback do not provide arbitrary new numerical perception-to-control code composition.
gap.stakes: Avoid new robot demonstrations/training for each compositional skill; precise coordinates and reactive conditions can matter to execution rather than only plan plausibility.
gap.method_response: Executable Python delegates exact arithmetic/geometry to libraries and composes perception/control primitives; hierarchical expansion permits additional code complexity within prompt limits.
gap.remaining_gap: No proof of safe/feasible behavior, incomplete real-world measurement, fixed primitive/perception limits, manual prompt design and unmeasured runtime overhead.
unresolved: Nearest-neighbor source versions and original-method details independently unverified: only focal paper's pinned discussion available within this assignment's reading boundary.
No comprehensive historical novelty search or base-model pretraining contamination audit; these cannot be inferred from missing search hits.

condition_checks.reason: Code versus NL and flat versus hierarchy comparisons exist; matched LLM-call/token budget not established.
Numerical geometry APIs and registered depth transform are described; simulator structured positions simplify perception; calibration/noise robustness not swept.
Lexical execution checks do not validate motion feasibility/safety. Feasible instructions are assumed; no MuJoCo/kinematic candidate checks claimed.
No frozen VLA staged into contact by this method; handwritten pick/place/navigation primitives rather than VLA steering.
No proposed invocation-aligned compact-tool training or student policy.
Perception and primitive limitations acknowledged; tight-contact success not tested. No failure-rate claim imported from later card sources.
Representation/hierarchy controls exist but prompt/history/compute contributions not fully separated; no basis to assert budget exhaustion occurred.
Four-model offline code-generation results show strength sensitivity; embodied effect measured only with default model.
No learned navigation-tool addition evaluated across backends.
No frozen learned VLA accessed with versus without playbook.
API/perception coverage is a stated bound, but invocation-trained tool data gaps are inapplicable.
Risk present: real-world evidence explicitly qualitative; no robot transfer rate inferred.

revision_proposals: No asset edited. Candidate distinction for future synthesis: one-shot language-compiled reactive code plus unresolved-name expansion is not the same feedback affordance as execution-diagnostic iterative coding-agent repair; K105 covers both at coarse operation level.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: LLM translates instructions to executable structured programs; interpreter and geometry libraries compute exact numerical subresults; robot APIs implement actions. This specializes delegation to physical policy composition.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: Reliable API contracts/calibration and adequate primitives are required. Interpreter semantics do not verify physical correctness. C25 verifier-guided construction is absent, hence no rs:C25 label; modern K105 diagnostic-retry variants are only partial analogues.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Fixed code model takes task comments/API hints/example code and emits new robot policies with no task-specific weight update; conditioning determines which primitives and numerical logic are composed.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: Task-conditioned code inference needs adequate pretrained model and prompt coverage. No new upstream training/shared-space substrate is proposed, so C03's tighter tactic is not asserted. Within-environment UI/UA tests are not quantitative cross-body transfer.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice, reading-derived; not an actual review of this paper

expectations.applies_when: Hierarchy/code representation is claimed to improve performance
expectations.reason: Flat-prompt HumanEval comparator addresses added prompting and hierarchy; robot task evaluation does not isolate hierarchy, persistence and arithmetic-library use one at a time, nor control added function-generation calls.

expectations.applies_when: General effectiveness of hierarchical code generation across model strengths
expectations.reason: Four-model RoboCodeGen and generalization analysis establish strength-dependence offline; no matched multi-backbone closed-loop robot comparison. No extrapolation to compact students.

expectations.applies_when: Practical alternative robot harness and additional hierarchical calls
expectations.reason: Complete fixed text gives models, temperatures and evaluation sampling modes, but no measured per-episode LLM calls/tokens/latency/USD including failures. This is absent reporting, not evidence that runtime is cheap.

expectations.applies_when: Historical agentic manipulation versus end-to-end policy claim; modern named-suite prescription is temporally inapplicable
expectations.reason: Contemporaneous CLIPort trained on 30k demonstrations is compared, with UI/UA perturbations and oracle/no-oracle termination disclosed. Requiring 2026 LIBERO-PRO/pi0.5 etc of a 2023 version is not applicable; no deduction for absent future baselines. Underlying fair stronger-policy comparison remains confounded by structured perception and training exposure.

expectations.applies_when: Demonstration of the system across real robot platforms / embodiment generality
expectations.reason: Drawing, manipulation and mobile robot demonstrations lack per-task counted success rates; authors explicitly limit quantitative robot evaluation to simulation. Allows demonstration claim but not quantified real robustness/transfer.

No matched LLM-call/turn/token/time cap for hierarchically generated functions versus flat generation; CLIPort ten-action and oracle stopping are disclosed, but disclosure is not equal interaction budget.

claims.text: Generated code supports compositional and spatial-geometric robot instruction following without new policy training.
claims.setting: Codex code-davinci-002, temperature 0; simulated UR5e tabletop, scripted object list/position access and pick/place API; seen/unseen instruction and attribute groups.
claims.baseline/control: CLIPort with 30k demonstrations; NL planner; Table VI explicitly separates oracle and ten-action non-oracle CLIPort. NL spatial-geometric N/A is not a measured failure rate.
claims.selection_vs_test: Appendix K lists prompt-eligible templates/attributes and separate UI/UA values. Authors engineer prompts; exact linked simulation prompt texts and development audit not in the PDF. No test-driven self-improvement claimed.
claims.result/denominator: 50 randomized trials per task template per evaluated scenario. Table III: CaP long-horizon SA-SI/UA-SI/UA-UI =97.2/97.6/80.0%; spatial-geometric =89.3/73.33/62.0%; NL long-horizon =86.4/88.0/64.0%. Table VI UA-UI all-task total=71.0%. Family means are not a single 50-trial denominator; no pooled numerator inferred.
counterevidence: Simulation uses structured scripted detection; CLIPort end-to-end data/perception differs.
Per-task success geometry/tolerances and checker reliability not explicit; no significance intervals.
K prose labels seen task 5 in both family ranges, while Table VI aggregate values align with distinct long-horizon/spatial groups; retain author's reported family means, do not invent pooled counts.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Authors report stronger within-environment template/attribute generalization for this modular code interface than these comparators; not robust visual transfer or causal proof that all gains derive from hierarchy.

claims.text: Hierarchical code generation improves robotics-themed and generic code correctness.
claims.setting: 37 RoboCodeGen functions with human-written tests; four LLMs; 164 HumanEval questions using code-davinci-002.
claims.baseline/control: Flat versus hierarchical; Appendix D additionally flat + two flat examples versus hierarchy + corresponding hierarchical examples. Historical code-davinci-001 scores are not same-backbone evidence.
claims.selection_vs_test: Greedy T=0 and sampled T=0.8 pass@N modes separate. Human-written tests score offline outputs; not available as a robot deployment policy selector.
claims.result/denominator: RoboCodeGen Table I davinci 81->95% over 37 functions; HumanEval Table V greedy 45.7 no-prompt /50.6 flat-prompt /53.0 hierarchical; sampled P@1 34.9/36.6/39.8%. Percentage rounding and pass@ estimators preclude fabricating integer counts from displayed values.
counterevidence: Hierarchical runtime introduces additional function-generation calls without equal-compute accounting.
Small cushman does not benefit uniformly on all generalization categories (IV A/Appendix E).
Offline code correctness does not establish robot-task success or motion safety.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Reported code benchmark improvements support a useful decomposition technique on capable code models; no independent reproduction, equal-compute optimality or safety guarantee.

claims.text: Code reasoning is better suited than natural-language reasoning for precise spatial computation.
claims.setting: Appendix C, 28 object-selection questions and 23 position-selection questions with provided coordinates; position answers correct within 1cm.
claims.baseline/control: Vanilla NL, CoT and executable LMP output.
claims.selection_vs_test: Fixed hand-built question sets and example prompts; no independent held-out construction audit or repetitions reported for this static diagnostic.
claims.result/denominator: Table IV author-reported object/position/total percentages: vanilla 39/30/35; CoT 68/48/58; LMP 96/100/98. Counts are questions, not physical trials.
counterevidence: Exact external computation and coordinate information are advantages of the proposed representation, not a capacity-matched no-tool model test.
No uncertainty or equal-token accounting; not a closed-loop robotics benchmark.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Evidence supports the numerical-computation mechanism in the tested static setting and explains part of the problem fit, not general embodied reasoning superiority.

claims.text: The formulation can instantiate policies across real robots and reactive low-level controllers.
claims.setting: UR5e drawing and tabletop manipulation; mobile 7-DoF-arm robot in a kitchen; toy CartPole and PyBullet impedance controller examples.
claims.baseline/control: Demonstrations, not paired counted robot baselines. Appendix M compares generated API-conditioned code examples, not evaluated robot transfer.
claims.selection_vs_test: Domain-specific APIs/prompts and known geometry; no untouched embodiment/scene evaluation cohort with counted outcomes.
claims.result/denominator: Qualitative examples and instruction lists only; no per-task physical success denominator.
counterevidence: Controller gain tuning from execution is unsupported; object detection and unique-identity restrictions persist.
Unfamiliar API adaptation explicitly brittle; demonstrations do not establish transfer level.
claims.allowed_conclusion: A multi-platform feasibility demonstration of language-compiled policies, not quantified physical reliability, safe deployment or cross-embodiment transfer.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported repeated simulated tabletop evaluations support within-environment instruction/attribute generalization of a frozen-Codex executable-code harness with scripted object-position access; offline controlled code benchmarks support hierarchical generation and precise computation. Multi-platform real-robot examples demonstrate feasibility, not counted reliability or transfer. No experiments independently reproduced here.
unresolved: Exact numerical simulator success predicates/tolerances and complete linked domain prompt contents are not in the fixed PDF extraction; Appendix C's 1cm criterion is only for the offline coordinate diagnostic.
Historical adjacent methods independently unverified and pretraining overlap unaudited.
No equal-call/token compute comparison, runtime-cost report, seed uncertainty, quantitative physical transfer or longitudinal retained-gain study.
assessment.reason_not_transfer: Both physical platforms use tailored APIs/prompts and qualitative demonstrations; simulation UI/UA is the same constructed scene/task environment with scripted structured perception. Anchors v2 prohibit treating privileged symbolic access or uncounted demonstrations as transfer.

G.reason: Specific important planner-to-controller expressivity/data bottleneck, with acknowledged nearby feedback-aware planners and explicit residual beyond fixed skills. Original neighbor versions not independently inspected; no exhaustive closest-frontier verification. Hence strong but not fully sourced 4-level lineage.
